title: 2008 Made Me a Millionaire. Pullbacks Like This Are Why
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: auto-captions garble 'Jensen Huang' as 'Jensen Wang', 'Anthropic' as 'Enthropic' and 'Palantir' as 'Palanteer'
summary: Brian (BWB) frames the November sell-off through his 2008 experience: pullbacks made him a millionaire. The Nasdaq-100 had fallen about 20% from its October high before a 7% single-day jump on Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, up almost 30% that day. He argues pullbacks are normal - the Nasdaq-100 has crossed into bear-market territory four times since 2015, and in 2018, 2020 and 2025 the bottom came within days, with gains of 26-54% six months later - while 2022 took 21 months because the Fed kept raising rates. Citing Nassim Taleb's Fooled by Randomness, he shows the Nasdaq-100 is up about 55% of days but about 80% of years and 89% of 10-year periods, which is why checking daily feels so bad. His filters for the seven stocks he is buying himself on this dip: big, cash-generative, self-funding growth and debt, and fallen at least as hard as the Nasdaq. Meta fails the filter (78% of operating cash spent on AI, $81B debt). He covers Nvidia (CUDA moat, ~75% gross margin, growth back above 100%, forward P/E about 11), Broadcom (AI now 56% of sales, two years of signed orders), Micron (HBM contracts covering over 35% of sales to 2030, P/E about 4), ASML (only EUV maker, sold out through 2027), TSMC (revenue up 41% on 10% wafer growth), Arista (growth back to 58% on open Ethernet) and Palantir (operating margin 1% to 47%, P/E about 64). His dollar-cost-average basket weights Nvidia about 25%, TSMC, Palantir and Broadcom about 15% each, and Micron, Arista and ASML about 10% each. Calls: NVDA BUY (flip from CONDITIONAL_BUY), MU BUY (flip from HOLD), AVGO, ASML, TSM, PLTR BUY reiterated, ANET BUY first tracked.

calls.stance_flip: Was CONDITIONAL_BUY on 15 Nov; now BUY.
calls.thesis: BUY - FLIP from CONDITIONAL_BUY (15 Nov, when he was waiting to see who would run Nvidia). Jensen's return answers that question, so he can look at reinvesting again; Nvidia is his biggest piece at ~25% of this seven-stock dollar-cost-average basket. CUDA moat (4M+ developers), ~75% gross margin, growth back above 100% after an 18-month slowdown, forward P/E ~11. Risks: Jensen's resignation scandal (affair, reported China-linked contact, board/DOJ investigations still open) and supplier commitments up ~40% in a quarter, mostly memory.
calls.base_case: The business is not broken; the ~47% drop was a scandal-driven overreaction and the stock recovers as the leadership question is settled.
calls.bull_case: CUDA lock-in plus edge computing (+42% YoY) keeps growth above 100% and the multiple re-rates.
calls.bear_case: Congressional/DOJ scrutiny of Jensen drags on, or the memory-supplier bet proves demand was overstated.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated - Broadcom is an anchor in his portfolio and he is adding all the way down (now on the way up); ~15% of the basket. AI chips are now ~56% of sales (from ~33% a year ago), ~2 years of sales already signed and waiting to be delivered, Anthropic on track to be its largest XPU customer in 2027, and VMware margins have recovered above pre-deal levels. Watch item: Broadcom promised to cover ~$71B of Anthropic's bills if Anthropic cannot pay, against ~$24B cash on hand.
calls.base_case: Nothing broke at Broadcom; the stock fell faster than the business changed and the AI order book carries growth.
calls.bull_case: Anthropic XPU volumes ramp and the VMware margin recovery compounds.
calls.bear_case: The Anthropic backstop is called on, or the June decision to hold (not raise) the AI forecast proves demand is topping.

calls.stance_flip: Was HOLD on 15 Nov; now BUY.
calls.thesis: BUY - FLIP from HOLD (15 Nov). He is buying Micron slowly as a smaller piece (~10% of the basket) and it stays small until the long-term contracts hold or expand. HBM is the change: only three makers worldwide, Micron the only US one; customers went from ~16 to 26 multi-year contracts in 3 months, now covering >35% of sales out to 2030. Sales grew >375% in a year, ~87% gross margin, P/E ~4 vs ~14 five-year average - but that low P/E can fool near a cycle top.
calls.base_case: Multi-year take-or-pay contracts stretch this cycle out; demand cannot be fulfilled today.
calls.bull_case: Contracts hold and expand, proving this cycle is structurally different from past memory busts.
calls.bear_case: The cycle ends like the others - in 2019 Micron's gross margin fell from ~61% to ~29% in a year - and heavy factory spending meets slowing price increases.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated - he is building into ASML over the next few months (~10% of the basket). Only company in the world that builds EUV lithography machines; current machines all but sold out through 2027, customer down payments up ~180% in 9 months, operating margin broke out to ~44% last quarter after four years stuck in the 30s. P/E ~25 vs ~34 five-year average. Catches: much of last quarter's cash came from down payments that will not repeat at that pace, and China fell from ~36% to ~20% of sales on export controls.
calls.base_case: Irreplaceable monopoly with a sold-out order book; growth has accelerated four quarters in a row.
calls.bull_case: The order backlog converts into sustained margin expansion as EUV demand compounds.
calls.bear_case: Down-payment cash normalises and China restrictions tighten further, capping the re-rating.

calls.video_title: 2008 Made Me a Millionaire. Pullbacks Like This Are Why
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated - he is adding to TSMC through whatever the market does next (~15% of the basket); his pricing ladder reads it undervalued. Wafer shipments +10% YoY but revenue +41% - pricing power nobody else can match on advanced chips - and gross margin climbed from ~53% to ~66% over 10 quarters. Advanced packaging is one of the tightest bottlenecks in AI and capacity is set to roughly double by 2028. Risks: Nvidia and Apple together are ~40% of sales, overseas fabs cost far more to run, and the CEO's 'prudent into 2027' comment hit chip stocks.
calls.base_case: The business is doing great and the stock was just pulled down with everything else; pricing power sustains the margin.
calls.bull_case: Packaging capacity doubles by 2028 and the smallest-node lead widens as rivals keep throwing out bad chips.
calls.bear_case: Customer concentration bites, or a 2027 demand slowdown meets expensive new overseas capacity.

calls.thesis: BUY first tracked - Arista Networks is one of the seven stocks he is dollar-cost-averaging into on this dip (~10% of the basket). Its edge is software: one operating system across every switch lets a giant customer run 100,000 processors as one machine. Growth slowed for 2 years to ~16% in 2024, then sped back up almost every quarter to ~58%, its fastest in ~12 years; management guides ~40% growth next year and ~100% AI-business growth. Pitch is open Ethernet versus Nvidia's proprietary networking.
calls.base_case: AI networking demand keeps compounding as data-centre scale grows and Ethernet stays the open standard.
calls.bull_case: The ~100% AI-business growth guide proves out and Arista takes share from proprietary networking.
calls.bear_case: Nvidia bundles its own networking so tightly with its processors that Arista's open-standard pitch loses traction.

calls.video_title: 2008 Made Me a Millionaire. Pullbacks Like This Are Why
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY Aug 2025) - Palantir is an anchor he keeps adding to here and there (~15% of the basket); his pricing ladder reads it fairly valued. For the first time ever its US business customers pay it more than the US government; operating margin went from ~1% in early 2023 to ~47% today and growth has sped up every quarter for 3 years. The ontology maps a customer's whole business so AI can act on it, and boot camps replace months-long trials. Downside is valuation: P/E ~64, the most expensive name on his list.
calls.base_case: Rock-solid growth continues and new contracts keep surfacing; he keeps adding on dips.
calls.bull_case: Commercial momentum compounds as the ontology becomes the standard way enterprises deploy AI.
calls.bear_case: At ~64x earnings the stock has no room for a growth stumble.
